segments.text:
The web transcript doesn't use a virtualization library at all. That turns out to be the cause, and it can be fixed with a package rather than more custom code. I haven't reproduced the stutter in a browser yet, so the diagnosis below comes from reading the code.

## What's actually there

`ThreadTranscript` renders every turn inside `Chat` (`packages/ui/src/ai/chat.tsx`). `Chat` wraps shadcn's `MessageScroller` (`@shadcn/react/message-scroller` 0.3.1). The "virtualization" is one CSS line on each item in `packages/ui/src/components/message-scroller.tsx:76`:

```
[contain-intrinsic-size:auto_10rem] [content-visibility:auto]
```

That tells the browser to skip rendering off-screen items and guess each one is 160px tall until it is drawn. A transcript opens at the bottom, so everything above has never been drawn and is sitting at that guess. When you scroll up:

1. A turn comes into view and gets its real height: a 2,000px tool block replaces a 160px placeholder.
2. Everything shifts. The browser's built-in scroll anchoring tries to correct for it. At the same time, shadcn's scroller has its own correction (it adds the difference to the scroll position, then nudges again on the next frame).
3. Those two corrections fight each other, so the view jumps. The stutter is each turn's markdown and code highlighting rendering at the moment it scrolls in.

## Does shadcn solve it?

No. `MessageScroller` handles keeping the view pinned to the bottom, the jump-to-latest button and anchoring to a message. It doesn't virtualize, and its own docs only suggest `content-visibility` as a speed tip. Combining the two is exactly the setup that jumps.

## The options

| Package | Fit for chat | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **virtua** (MIT, ~3 kB) | Built for this | Measures items itself and corrects the scroll position when items above you change size, which is the exact case here. It also has a mode for loading older messages above without a jump. Used by several AI chat UIs. |
| **@virtuoso.dev/message-list** | Purpose-built for AI chatbots | The most complete option, but it's a commercial license with a paid key. |
| **react-virtuoso** (MIT) | Good, has a reverse mode | Heavier. Its free tier isn't the chat-specific product. |
| **@tanstack/react-virtual** (already a dependency) | Poor for chat | It doesn't correct for items resizing above the viewport by default. `deprecated/web` worked around that with `scroll-compensation.ts` and `idle-premeasure.tsx`, which is the custom wiring you're describing. |

## The usual approach in chat apps

- Use one library that measures each item, owns the scroll position and corrects it when items above the viewport change size. Don't use CSS-only virtualization.
- Give the list stable keys (turn ids), which `turnsOf` already does.
- Let one system own the scroll. Here that means virtua does both the bottom-pinning and the anchoring, and `MessageScroller` goes away.
- Keep the jump-to-latest button and the jump when you send a message. Both are small additions on top of virtua.

## What I'd do

Replace `MessageScroller` and the `content-visibility` classes inside `Chat` with virtua's `VList`, keeping the `Chat`/`ChatItem` API. That way `thread-transcript.tsx` barely changes, and the agents panel's custom `useStickToBottom` with TanStack can move to the same component.

Before that, there's a one-line check: delete the `content-visibility` classes and scroll a long transcript. If the jumping stops (and it just renders more slowly), the diagnosis is confirmed.

Should I go ahead with virtua, or do you want the commercial Virtuoso message list instead?

const NEAR_BOTTOM_THRESHOLD = 48

interface ScrollMetrics {
  scrollTop: number
  clientHeight: number
  scrollHeight: number
}

export function isNearBottom({ scrollTop, clientHeight, scrollHeight }: ScrollMetrics): boolean {
